mechanism_narrative: The Federal Funds rate is a leading indicator of equity market returns; the historical relationship between low Federal Funds rates and positive S&P 500 returns is so strong that the signal is always active and predicts positive returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 8.0%, it signals a weak labor market that often precedes a Federal Reserve rate cut, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances when UNRATE > 8.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in GDP growth (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) signals a weakening demand environment that often triggers a policy response, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between GDPC1 and HOUST does not produce positive 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances where both series decline by more than 1% from their 3-month moving average.

mechanism_narrative: In high inflation regimes (CPIAUCSL > 3.0% annually), the Federal Reserve is likely to maintain a restrictive monetary policy, which often leads to positive S&P 500 returns as the market prices in the eventual normalization of policy.
failure_condition: In periods where CPIAUCSL > 230.0, the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in more than 55% of instances, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 95.0 (2017=100), it signals a weakening economy that often leads to policy stimulus, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances when INDPRO < 95.0.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) and rise in CPI (CPIAUCSL) signals a 'transitory' inflation environment where the Fed is likely to keep rates low, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The interaction between FEDFUNDS decline and CPIAUCSL rise does not produce positive 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances where FEDFUNDS falls by more than 0.1% and CPIAUCSL rises by more than 0.5% from the previous month.

mechanism_narrative: In high unemployment regimes (UNRATE > 8.0%), the Federal Reserve is likely to maintain an accommodative monetary policy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In periods where UNRATE > 8.0%, the S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in more than 55% of instances, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When housing starts (HOUST) fall below 650.0 (thousands of units), it signals a weakening housing market that often precedes a policy response, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5-day returns in more than 55% of instances when HOUST < 650.0.
